q: Which of the following surveys/data is the Owner responsible for furnishing (or directing the Architect to obtain at the Owner's expense), per Sec. 6.4?
o: A certified survey of the site (topographical/relocation surveys, boundaries, utility lines, soil investigations, etc.)
The Architect's professional indemnity insurance
The building permit application form only
The Contractor's performance bond
n: Sec. 6.4 requires the Owner to furnish or direct the Architect to obtain, at the Owner's expense, a certified survey of the site covering topographical/relocation data, boundaries, utility lines, zoning compliance, and soil investigations. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.4)

q: The Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses method of compensation (Sec. 5.2) is applicable only to what kind of work, and why?
o: Only construction supervision work
Purely creative design work, since it best rewards artistic talent
Non-creative work such as accounting, secretarial, research and data gathering - because the value of creative design cannot be measured by time spent
Government projects exclusively
n: Sec. 5.2 states this cost-based method applies only to non-creative work (accounting, secretarial, research, data gathering, report preparation, etc.) since creative design's value cannot be measured by hours spent. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 5.2)

q: Under Sec. 2.5.2.a and Sec. 33 of R.A. No. 9266, who owns the Bid Documents furnished for a competitive bidding, and what may bidders be required to post?
o: Ownership passes to the government upon submission of the bid
The Architect retains sole ownership and copyright; a bond may be required to assure return of the documents
The Owner retains sole ownership; bidders keep the documents permanently once bid opens
The winning Contractor owns the documents upon award; no bond is required
n: Sec. 2.5.2.a states the Bid Documents are the intellectual property of the Architect (Sec. 33, R.A. No. 9266) and must be returned; a bond may be required to assure their return. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 2.5.2.a)

q: A proposed public market and a warehouse are being classified under SPP Document 202's project classification. Which Group do they fall under?
o: Group 5 - monumental buildings
Group 3 - buildings of exceptional character and complexity
Group 1 - buildings of the simplest utilization and character
Group 2 - buildings of moderate complexity
n: Sec. 4.1 (Group 1) lists Public Markets and Warehouses among buildings of the simplest utilization and character. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 4.1)

q:
Architect Reyes is engaged under the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses method (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 5.2) for a small renovation involving non-creative, cost-based work. Her own rate is P800/hour for 40 hours logged; her Consultant's rate is P600/hour for 20 hours; her Technical Staff's rate is P300/hour for 60 hours. The parties agree on a multiplier (M) of 2.0 to cover overhead and profit. Reimbursable expenses (R) for the engagement total P15,000.

Suppose the parties had instead agreed on the maximum multiplier allowed under Sec. 5.2 (2.5) rather than 2.0. What would the Fee have been?
n: At the maximum allowable multiplier of 2.5, Fee = P62,000 x 2.5 = P155,000. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 5.2)
scenario: Architect Reyes is engaged under the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses method (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 5.2) for a small renovation involving non-creative, cost-based work. Her own rate is P800/hour for 40 hours logged; her Consultant's rate is P600/hour for 20 hours; her Technical Staff's rate is P300/hour for 60 hours. The parties agree on a multiplier (M) of 2.0 to cover overhead and profit. Reimbursable expenses (R) for the engagement total P15,000.

q: Per Sec. 7.1, on what is the Architect's Fee based, and what happens if the Architect must render additional services?
o: The Fee is based on the Project Construction Cost; additional services require additional compensation
Additional services are always absorbed within the original fee at no extra cost
The Fee is a fixed government-set amount regardless of services rendered
The Fee is based solely on the Architect's years of experience
n: Sec. 7.1 states the Architect's Fee is based on the Project Construction Cost, and where the Architect renders additional services, additional compensation shall be required. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 7.1)

q: Which of the following is NOT part of the Architect's duties during the Contract Document Phase (Sec. 2.4)?
o: Preparing Technical Specifications describing type and quality of materials and manner of construction
Updating the SPPCC based on changes in scope, requirements, or market conditions
Awarding the construction contract to the winning bidder
Preparing complete Contract Documents consisting of detailed designs and construction drawings
n: Awarding the construction contract occurs during the Bidding or Negotiation Phase (Sec. 2.5.1.b: "assists the Owner...to awarding of the construction contract"), not the Contract Document Phase, whose duties are described in Sec. 2.4.1, 2.4.2 and 2.4.4. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 2.4 and Sec. 2.5.1.b)

q: If a project needs the services of acoustic/illumination specialists, mural painters, or sculptors (Sec. 7.2), who recommends these to the Owner, and what fee does the Architect receive?
o: The Contractor recommends them, and the Architect receives no additional compensation
The PRBoA assigns them directly and bills the Owner
The Owner sources them independently with no Architect involvement or fee
The Architect recommends them for the Owner's approval, and is entitled to a coordination fee for these services (paid separately by the Owner)
n: Sec. 7.2 states other services (acoustic/illumination specialists, mural painters, sculptors, etc.) are recommended by the Architect for the Owner's approval, paid for separately by the Owner, subject to a coordination fee payable to the Architect. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 7.2)

q: If the Owner requires the services of specialist consultants, per Sec. 7.9 with whose consent must they be engaged, and how is their cost treated relative to the Architect's fee?
o: Engaged with the Contractor's consent only
Engaged with the PRBoA's prior approval, billed to the Architect
Engaged with the Architect's consent; their cost is paid separately by the Owner and shall NOT be deducted from the Architect's fee
Engaged without needing anyone's consent; their cost is deducted from the Architect's fee
n: Sec. 7.9 requires specialist consultants to be engaged with the Architect's consent, with their cost paid separately by the Owner and not deducted from the Architect's fee. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 7.9)

q: An Architect notices during a routine periodic site visit that the Contractor's masonry work does not conform to the Contract Documents. What is the Architect's obligation per Sec. 2.6.3?
o: Immediately terminate the Contractor's contract personally
Say nothing since the Architect is not required to conduct continuous supervision
Pay for the corrective work out of the Architect's own fee
Report to the Client the defects/deficiencies noted and condemn work found failing to conform to the Contract Documents
n: Sec. 2.6.3 requires the Architect, on the basis of site-visit observations, to report defects/deficiencies to the Client and condemn work failing to conform to the Contract Documents. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 2.6.3)

q: An Owner wants to hand over materials procurement decisions and issue direct instructions to the Contractor without going through the Architect. Is this consistent with the Owner's responsibilities under SPP Document 202?
o: No - all instructions must instead go through the specialist consultants
Yes - Owners may always bypass the Architect for efficiency
No - Sec. 6.3 requires the Owner to issue orders to the Contractor only through the Architect
Yes - but only for Group 1 projects
n: Sec. 6.3 requires the Owner to route orders to the General Contractor only through the Architect, to avoid unreasonable delay and preserve the Architect's oversight role. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3)

q: Architect Bautista's established office, per her letterhead, is in Quezon City. The Owner requires her to render services at a project site 80 kilometers (straight-line/radial distance) away. Under Sec. 7.4, what may be charged to the Owner?
o: The full cost of relocating her office temporarily
Nothing extra - this distance is still within the free-travel radius
A per diem only if the distance exceeds 100 kilometers, not 50
A per diem plus traveling and living expenses, since the site is beyond the 50.0-kilometer threshold from her established office
n: Sec. 7.4 provides that a per diem plus traveling and living expenses is chargeable to the Owner whenever the Architect must perform services beyond 50.0 kilometers (air, straight-line or radial distance) from the office shown on the Architect's letterhead. At 80km, this threshold is exceeded. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 7.4)

q: How does "Project Development Cost" (Sec. 7.18) differ from "Project Construction Cost" (Sec. 7.17)?
o: Project Development Cost additionally includes all professional fees, permits, clearances, utilities, cost of acquiring the site/lot, and cost of money, on top of construction cost
Project Development Cost is always smaller than Project Construction Cost
They are simply two different names for the exact same amount
Project Development Cost excludes construction cost altogether
n: Sec. 7.18 defines Project Development Cost as including the cost of construction PLUS all professional fees, permits, clearances, utilities, cost of acquiring the project site/lot, and cost of money - broader than the PCC alone. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 7.17, 7.18)

q: Per Sec. 6.8, which taxes on the Architect's services rendered on the project must the Owner pay?
o: Only local government taxes, never national taxes
Only VAT; all other taxes including income tax are Owner's responsibility as well
No taxes at all - these are always for the Architect's own account
All taxes, including VAT, that government may impose as a result of the services rendered, but NOT including the Architect's income tax
n: Sec. 6.8 requires the Owner to pay all reimbursable expenses and taxes including VAT that government may impose on the Architect as a result of services rendered, but excluding the Architect's income tax. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.8)

q: Who pays for additional sets of Contract Documents beyond what is already provided, per Sec. 7.5?
o: The Architect's professional liability insurer
The Architect, out of the basic professional fee
The Owner
The Contractor
n: Sec. 7.5 states the Owner shall pay the Architect for additional sets of Contract Documents. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 7.5)

q: Which of the following is explicitly EXCLUDED from the Project Construction Cost (PCC), per Sec. 7.17?
o: The building's plumbing/sanitary and electrical fixtures
The mechanical equipment, elevators, and escalators
Fees for the Architect, the Engineer, the Specialist Consultants, or the salaries of construction inspectors
The fire protection, alarm and communications/electronic systems
n: Sec. 7.17 explicitly states the PCC does not include any fees for the Architect, the Engineer, the Specialist Consultants, or the salaries of construction inspectors, while items like fixtures, equipment, elevators, and alarm/communication systems ARE part of the PCC. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 7.17)

q: Per Sec. 6.3, through whom should the Owner issue orders to the General Contractor?
o: Through the Project/Construction Manager exclusively
Only through the Architect
Through the specialist consultants
Directly to the Contractor at any time, bypassing the Architect
n: Sec. 6.3 states the Owner should issue orders to the General Contractor only through the Architect, to avoid unreasonable delay caused by miscommunication. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.3)

q: Under Sec. 6.6 and 6.7, besides the Architect's own fee, what other costs must the Owner arrange and pay for?
o: Design/consulting services for acoustic, communication, electronic and other specialty systems, plus legal, auditing, insurance and counseling services as required
The Architect's professional license renewal fees
The Architect's personal income tax
The PRC board examination fees of the Architect's staff
n: Sec. 6.6 requires the Owner to pay for design/consulting services on acoustic, communication, electronic and other specialty systems, and Sec. 6.7 requires the Owner to arrange and pay for legal, auditing, insurance, counseling and similar services. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.6, 6.7)

q: What general rule under Sec. 7.7 governs compensation when the Architect's work is abandoned or suspended in whole or in part, at any stage (not just after Contract Documents)?
o: The Architect must refund any fees already received
The Owner shall pay the Architect for services rendered corresponding to the amount due at the stage of suspension or abandonment
The Owner pays only 10% of the fee regardless of stage reached
The Architect forfeits all fees if the project does not reach construction
n: Sec. 7.7 states that if the Architect's work is abandoned or suspended in whole or in part, the Owner pays for the services rendered corresponding to the amount due at that stage. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 7.7)

q: In the Project Definition Phase, the Architect informs the Owner of which two things, per Sec. 2.1?
o: The final construction cost and the contractor's profit margin
The zoning classification and the applicable real property tax
The building permit fee schedule and the requisite bonds
The technical requirements of the project and the concomitant professional fees
n: Sec. 2.1 states that in this phase the Architect informs the Owner of the technical requirements of the project and the concomitant professional fees. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 2.1)

q: Where is the Architect's Fee based on a Percentage (%) of Project Construction Cost (PCC) specifically detailed, per Sec. 5.1?
o: In R.A. No. 9266 itself, Sec. 5
In the Architect's Guidelines
In SPP Document 203 only
In the National Building Code IRR
n: Sec. 5.1 states the Architect's Fee based on the PCC shall be detailed in the Architect's Guidelines. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 5.1)

q: A foreign Architect wishes to render architectural services for a project on Philippine soil. Which of the following is a specific requirement under Sec. 1.1.2 of SPP Document 202?
o: Obtain accreditation from the Bureau of Immigration only, with no local counterpart required
Simply register the project with the local government unit
File a notarized waiver with the PRC exempting compliance with Sec. 37 of R.A. No. 9266
Secure a Temporary/Special Permit (TSP) and work permit from DOLE, and work with a local counterpart Registered and Licensed Architect (RLA)
n: Sec. 1.1.2 requires a foreign architect to secure a TSP and work permit from DOLE and to work in collaboration with a local counterpart Architect who is a Registered and Licensed Architect (RLA) under Philippine law. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 1.1.2)

q:
On a separate project, Architect Cruz and the Owner agreed that P200,000 of the fee remained payable for the Construction Phase. Because the building was to be erected in phases, actual construction work was suspended for eight (8) months before it resumed.

Given the 8-month suspension (exceeding the 6-month threshold), what is the adjusted fee for the remaining works under Sec. 7.8?
n: Since the suspension (8 months) exceeds the 6-month threshold in Sec. 7.8, the fee for the remaining works is doubled: P200,000 x 2 = P400,000. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 7.8)

q: When does the Architect's regular design service work begin and end, per SPP Document 202?
o: Begins upon issuance of the building permit; ends upon final Certificate of Payment
Begins at the signing of the Owner-Architect agreement; ends at submission of the SPPCC
Begins at project inception when the Owner outlines requirements; ends when the contractor turns over the completed project to the Owner
Begins at the Schematic Design Phase; ends at the Bidding Phase
n: Sec. 1.2.2 states the Architect's work starts at the inception of the project when the Owner outlines requirements, and ends only when the general contractor or builder turns over the completed project to the Owner. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 1.2.2)

q: A DTI-registered Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) firm in the Philippines wants to provide architectural design services for a building project located on Philippine soil for an overseas client. Under Sec. 1.1.3, is this allowed?
o: Yes, as long as the firm is DTI- or SEC-registered, regardless of PRC registration
Yes, since the client is based overseas, Philippine registration rules do not apply
No, unless the firm is a PRC-registered architectural firm satisfying Sec. 37 of R.A. No. 9266 and its IRR
No, BPO/KPO firms may never provide any architectural-related service under any circumstance
n: Sec. 1.1.3 states BPO/KPO firms are not authorized to provide architectural services for Philippine-soil projects unless they are PRC-registered architectural firms satisfying Sec. 37 of R.A. No. 9266. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 1.1.3)

q: If, instead, construction on that same project had been suspended for only four (4) months, would the doubling rule of Sec. 7.8 apply to the remaining fee?
o: No - doubling only applies when suspension exceeds six (6) months; four months would not trigger it
Yes - any suspension automatically doubles the fee
No - suspension of any length has no effect on fees under this SPP
Yes - but only the fee would be reduced, not doubled
n: Sec. 7.8 only doubles the fee for remaining works when the suspension of construction exceeds six (6) months; a four-month suspension would not meet that threshold. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 7.8)

q: If the Owner wants the Architect to design movable/fixed cabinets and other architectural interior (AI) elements or site development plan (SDP) components, per Sec. 7.10 how is the Architect compensated for this separate service, and under which other SPP Document is the basis provided?
o: No additional compensation is allowed for these items
The Owner pays the Architect in addition to the regular fee, based on Project Construction Cost as provided under SPP Document 203
It is compensated solely under the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses method
This is included free within the Group 4 classification fee
n: Sec. 7.10 provides that for AI, SDP, and similar items, the Owner pays the Architect in addition to the Architect's fee, with compensation based on the Project Construction Cost as provided under SPP Document 203. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 7.10)

q: Under the Per Diem, Honorarium Plus Reimbursable Expenses method (Sec. 5.5), which of the following activities is specifically listed as compensable this way?
o: Issuing the final Certificate of Payment
Preparing the Design Development documents
Conducting ocular inspection of possible project sites
Preparing the complete Contract Documents
n: Sec. 5.5.2 lists "conducting ocular inspection of possible project sites" as one of the activities for which the Architect may be paid on a per diem and honorarium basis plus out-of-pocket expenses. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 5.5.2)

q: Per Sec. 5.2, within what range may the multiplier (M) used in the Direct Personnel Expenses method fall?
n: Sec. 5.2 states the multiplier ranges from 1.5 to 2.5 depending on the office set-up, overhead, experience of the Architect, and complexity of the project. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 5.2)

q: In the Contract Document Phase, how many sets of construction drawings and technical specifications does the Architect submit to the Owner for purposes of obtaining a building permit, per Sec. 2.4.3?
o: Seven (7) sets
Three (3) sets
Ten (10) sets
Five (5) sets
n: Sec. 2.4.3 requires the Architect to submit to the Owner seven (7) sets of all construction drawings and technical specifications for purposes of obtaining a building permit. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 2.4.3)

q: How does the Architect's role differ between a competitive bid/procurement and a negotiated contract, per Sec. 2.5.2-2.5.3?
o: For negotiated contracts, the Owner alone conducts all negotiations without Architect involvement
For negotiated contracts, the Architect performs similar functions but negotiates with one Contractor instead of many bidders
For negotiated contracts, no Bid Documents are ever prepared at all
For competitive bids, the Architect has no role once bidding opens
n: Sec. 2.5.3 states that for negotiated contracts, the Architect performs similar functions as in competitive bidding (Sec. 2.5.2) but negotiates with a single Contractor rather than multiple bidders. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 2.5.3)

q: SPP Document 202 is part of the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of which law, and which older document does it replace?
o: P.D. 1096; replaces the 1979 UAP Doc. 202
R.A. No. 9266; replaces the 2004 UAP Doc. 202
R.A. No. 545; replaces the 1979 UAP Doc. 203
R.A. No. 9266; replaces the 1979 UAP Doc. 202
n: The document's header states it is part of the IRR of R.A. No. 9266 (The Architecture Act of 2004) and that it replaces the 1979 UAP Doc. 202. (Source: SPP Document 202, header)

q:
Architect Cruz completed the entire Contract Documents phase (detailed designs, construction drawings and technical specifications) for a project with a total agreed professional fee of P1,000,000. Before construction could start, the Owner decided to abandon the project altogether.

Per Sec. 7.7, completion of the Detailed Design and Contract Documents Phase is equivalent to what percentage of the Architect's total work?
o: One hundred percent (100%)
Seventy-five percent (75%)
Fifty percent (50%)
Ninety percent (90%)
n: Sec. 7.7 states that once the Architect has prepared all Detailed Design and Contract Documents, this is equivalent to ninety percent (90%) of the Architect's work. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 7.7)

q: What must the Owner do, per Sec. 6.9, upon observing or becoming aware of anything that may impair the successful implementation of the project?
o: Withhold all payments until the Architect personally investigates
Immediately terminate the Contractor's contract
File a complaint with the PRBoA
Give prompt written notice to the Architect
n: Sec. 6.9 requires the Owner to give prompt written notice to the Architect upon observing or becoming aware of anything that may impair successful project implementation. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 6.9)

q: What does Sec. 5.6 ("Mixed Methods of Compensation") provide regarding how a project's compensation method should be determined?
o: Only one method may ever be used per project, chosen at contract signing and never combined
More than one method of compensation may apply on a project; each project should be examined to determine the most appropriate method
Mixed methods are prohibited under the IRR of R.A. No. 9266
Government projects must always mix Lump Sum with Percentage of PCC
n: Sec. 5.6 provides that the SPP allows more than one method of compensation on a project, and each project should be examined to determine the most appropriate method. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 5.6)

q: Single-detached residences, single-attached or duplex homes, row-houses/shop-houses, small apartment houses, and townhouses fall under which project classification Group?
o: Group 2
Group 9
Group 7
Group 4
n: Sec. 4.4 (Group 4) covers residences (single-detached, single-attached or duplex; row-houses or shop-houses), small apartment houses and townhouses. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 4.4)

q: Per Sec. 7.16, who must approve the size, design and content of signboards placed at the project site by the General Contractor, sub-contractors, jobbers and dealers during construction?
o: No approval is required during construction
The Architect
The Owner's building lessee
The local government's building official only
n: Sec. 7.16 states that all signboards placed at the project site during construction shall be approved by the Architect as to size, design and contents. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 7.16)

q: An Owner asks the Architect to design built-in cabinets, special fittings, screens, counters, and architectural interiors, plus development planning. Under which Group is this classified?
o: Group 8
Group 10
Group 1
Group 4
n: Sec. 4.8 (Group 8) covers projects involving extensive detail such as built-in components/elements, built-in equipment, special fittings, screens, counters, architectural interiors (AI), and development planning and/or design. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 4.8)

q: If the Owner orders changes to the design after the Architect's outputs have already been approved, per Sec. 7.6 who bears the cost of the resulting additional professional services?
o: The cost is split equally between Owner and Architect automatically
The Architect absorbs all costs of Owner-initiated changes
The Owner, who shall pay the Architect for extra time, resources/drafting, or other office expenses
The Contractor, since changes affect the construction schedule
n: Sec. 7.6 states that if the Architect renders additional services due to changes ordered by the Owner after approval of outputs, the Owner shall pay the Architect for extra time, resources/drafting, or other office expenses. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 7.6)

q: How does Group 6 differ from Group 7 in the SPP Document 202 project classification?
o: Group 6 covers alterations, while Group 7 covers new construction only
Group 6 covers residences only, while Group 7 covers commercial buildings only

Group 6 covers plans/Contract Documents re-used for repetitive construction of similar buildings (not necessarily on one site), while Group 7 is specifically a housing project on a single site using one set of plans
Group 6 and Group 7 are identical in scope
n: Sec. 4.6 (Group 6) covers projects where plans/Contract Documents are re-used for repetitive construction of similar buildings without amending drawings/specifications, while Sec. 4.7 (Group 7) is the specific case of a housing project on a single site with one set of plans. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 4.6, 4.7)

q:
On a separate project, Architect Cruz and the Owner agreed that P200,000 of the fee remained payable for the Construction Phase. Because the building was to be erected in phases, actual construction work was suspended for eight (8) months before it resumed.

Under Sec. 7.8, what happens to the fee for the remaining works when suspension of construction exceeds six (6) months?
o: The fee for the remaining works is reduced by half
The fee for the remaining works shall be doubled
The Architect forfeits the remaining fee entirely
The fee remains exactly the same regardless of suspension length
n: Sec. 7.8 provides that when suspension of construction exceeds a period of six (6) months, the fee for the remaining works shall be doubled. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 7.8)

q: According to Sec. 1.1.4, what may cause the Architect's listed outputs under this SPP to be expanded or increased?
o: Never - the outputs are fixed regardless of project or Architect
Depending on the project requirements or the Architect's experience, capabilities and specialization/s
Only if the Board issues a special resolution for that specific project
Only when the project cost exceeds P100 million
n: Sec. 1.1.4 provides that the Architect's outputs may be expanded or increased depending on the project requirements or the Architect's experience, capabilities and specialization/s. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 1.1.4)

q: Under Sec. 4, on what basis is professional architectural work classified into Groups?
o: The number of storeys of the building alone
The nationality of the Owner
The total floor area of the project alone
The degree of complexity and creative skill required to meet the Client's requirements within technical, functional, economic and aesthetic constraints
n: Sec. 4 states architectural work is classified according to the degree of complexity and creative skill required to meet the Client's requirements within technical, functional, economic, and aesthetic constraints. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 4)

q:
Architect Cruz completed the entire Contract Documents phase (detailed designs, construction drawings and technical specifications) for a project with a total agreed professional fee of P1,000,000. Before construction could start, the Owner decided to abandon the project altogether.

Given the 90% rule under Sec. 7.7, how much compensation is Architect Cruz entitled to receive for the abandoned project?
n: Since the Owner failed to implement the plans/documents after the Contract Documents Phase was completed (equivalent to 90% of the work), the Architect is entitled to 90% of the agreed fee: P1,000,000 x 0.90 = P900,000. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 7.7)

q: A hospital, a hotel, and an airport terminal are being classified under SPP Document 202. Which Group applies?
o: Group 3 - buildings of exceptional character and complexity of plan/design
Group 2 - buildings of moderate complexity
Group 9 - alterations and renovations
Group 1 - buildings of the simplest utilization
n: Sec. 4.3 (Group 3) lists Hospitals & Medical Buildings, Hotels, and Airports/Terminals among buildings of exceptional character and complexity. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 4.3)

q: If portions of a building are erected at different periods, increasing the construction period and the Architect's burden of services, what does Sec. 7.8 say about charges for the Construction Phase?
o: Charges pertaining to services rendered during the Construction Phase shall be adjusted proportionately
Only the Contractor's charges are adjusted, never the Architect's
Charges remain fixed at the original contract amount with no adjustment
The Architect must absorb the extra burden without added compensation
n: Sec. 7.8 states that if portions of the building are erected at different periods, increasing construction period and the Architect's burden of services, charges for Construction Phase services shall be adjusted proportionately. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 7.8)

q: While SPP Document 202 refers specifically to the individual professional practice of the Architect as a natural person, to whom may it also apply?
o: Engineering firms without any architect-in-charge
Only foreign architecture firms operating abroad
Only government agencies employing architects
The Architect's group practice as part of a DTI-registered sole proprietorship or SEC-registered partnership/corporation
n: Sec. 1.1.1 extends applicability to the Architect's "group practice" as part of a juridical entity (DTI-registered sole proprietorship or SEC-registered partnership/corporation), subject to full compliance with Sec. 37 of R.A. No. 9266. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 1.1.1)

q: If the Owner furnishes materials for the project below their market cost, how is the cost of that material and its installation labor treated for purposes of computing the PCC, per Sec. 7.17?
o: It shall nonetheless be computed on the basis of current, fair market value costs
It is excluded from the PCC entirely since the Owner supplied it
It is computed at the below-market price actually paid by the Owner
It is computed at zero cost since no cash changed hands
n: Sec. 7.17 provides that even if materials/labor are furnished by the Owner below market cost, they shall nonetheless be computed on the basis of current (fair market value) costs for PCC purposes. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 7.17)

q: In regular practice, in what capacity does the Architect act toward the Owner, Client, or Proponent?
o: As the Contractor's exclusive agent
As a co-owner of the finished structure
As an independent regulator of the project
As the Owner's/Client's/Proponent's Adviser and/or Representative
n: Sec. 1.2.1 states that in regular practice, the Architect acts as the Owner's/Client's/Proponent's Adviser and/or Representative, translating the Owner's needs into spaces and forms. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 1.2.1)

q: The Schematic Design Phase (Sec. 2.2) involves the preparation of what kind of studies, and results in what deliverable regarding cost?
o: Schematic design studies leading to conceptual plans, culminating in a Statement of the Probable Project Construction Cost (SPPCC)
Bid abstracts, culminating in a notice of award
As-built drawings, culminating in a warranty schedule
Detailed structural computations, culminating in a final bill of quantities
n: Sec. 2.2 describes schematic design studies leading to conceptual plans, and Sec. 2.2.3 has the Architect submit a Statement of the Probable Project Construction Cost (SPPCC) based on current cost parameters. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 2.2, 2.2.3)

q: A client merely asks an Architect for a technical opinion and clarification on an architectural matter, without any design or drawing output. What Group covers this engagement?
o: Group 8 - extensive detail projects
This is outside the scope of any Group and cannot be compensated
Group 1 - simplest utilization buildings
Group 10 - the Architect renders opinion or gives advice, clarification or explanation on technical matters
n: Sec. 4.10 (Group 10) covers engagements where the Architect is engaged to render opinion or give advice, clarifications, or explanation on technical matters pertaining to architectural works. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 4.10)

q: Per Sec. 7.13, is the Architect's Fee described as a gross or a net amount, and who bears applicable government taxes (other than income tax) arising from the Architect's services?
o: Fees under this SPP are always tax-exempt
A net amount, with all taxes including income tax paid by the Owner
A gross amount already inclusive of all taxes, paid by the Architect
A net amount; the national and/or local government taxes (exclusive of income tax) shall be paid by the Owner
n: Sec. 7.13 states the Architect's Fee is a net amount, and any tax (exclusive of income tax) imposed on the Architect due to the project's services shall be paid by the Owner. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 7.13)

q: The Lump Sum or Fixed Fee method of compensation (Sec. 5.4) is noted as being especially applicable to what kind of projects, and why?
o: Group 10 opinion/advisory engagements only
Foreign-funded projects only, due to currency conversion issues
Government projects, since they entail more paper work and time-consuming efforts
Private residential projects, since owners prefer simplicity
n: Sec. 5.4 states this method may be applied to government projects since they entail more paper work and time-consuming efforts. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 5.4)

q: Per Sec. 7.15, what must the Owner furnish the Architect during and upon completion of construction?
o: Nothing - cost records are the Architect's sole responsibility to compile
A notarized waiver releasing the Architect from liability
A copy of the Contractor's tax returns
A copy of the records/summary of expenses, labor, services, materials, equipment and fixtures used in the construction
n: Sec. 7.15 requires the Owner to furnish the Architect a copy of expense records during construction, and a summary of all cost of labor, services, materials, equipment and fixtures upon completion. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 7.15)

q: Under Sec. 7.14 and Sec. 33 of R.A. No. 9266, who owns the designs, drawings, models, specifications and other contract documents prepared and sealed by the Architect, even if the work is never executed?
o: They automatically become the Owner's exclusive property once signed and sealed
They become public domain works usable by anyone
Ownership transfers to the Contractor upon groundbreaking
They remain the intellectual property and documents of the Architect
n: Sec. 7.14 states these instruments of service are the intellectual property and documents of the Architect (Sec. 33, R.A. No. 9266), whether or not the work is executed, and may not be reproduced/used elsewhere without a written agreement with the Architect. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 7.14)

q: During the Construction Phase, is the Architect required to provide continuous 8-hour on-site supervision, per Sec. 2.6.3?
o: No supervision of any kind is required from the Architect during construction
Yes, but only for projects classified under Group 3
No - the Architect makes periodic site visits and is not required to render exhaustive/continuous 8-hour on-site supervision
Yes, full-time 8-hour supervision is always mandatory for the Architect personally
n: Sec. 2.6.3 states the Architect makes periodic site visits and shall not be required to make exhaustive or continuous 8-hour on-site supervision, nor be held responsible for the Contractor's failure to follow the Contract Documents. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 2.6.3)

q: During the Design Development Phase, what does the Architect prepare in addition to plans, elevations, sections, and outline specifications, per Sec. 2.3?
o: The final building permit and occupancy permit
A signed construction contract with the winning bidder
A diagrammatic layout of construction systems and an updated SPPCC
The notice to proceed and performance bond
n: Sec. 2.3.3-2.3.4 require a diagrammatic layout of construction systems and an updated SPPCC for submission to the Owner during the Design Development Phase. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 2.3.3, 2.3.4)

q: An Owner wants full-time (8-hour) construction supervision beyond the Architect's normal periodic site visits. What does Sec. 2.6.5 provide?
o: The Architect must personally provide this at no extra cost as part of regular design services
This service is legally prohibited under R.A. No. 9266
A separate full-time supervisor shall be hired and agreed upon by Owner and Architect, with fees covered separately under the applicable SPP Document on Full-Time Supervision
The Contractor must supply this supervisor free of charge
n: Sec. 2.6.5 provides that if more extensive inspection or full-time supervision is required, a separate full-time supervisor is hired and paid subject to conditions in the SPP Document on Full-Time Supervision, with fees covered separately. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 2.6.5)

q: Under Sec. 3, what are the two ways an Architect, as Lead Professional, may enter into contract with the Owner together with other engineering/allied professionals?
o: A single contract with sub-consultancy contracts between the Architect and other professionals, OR separate contracts executed directly between the Owner and each professional
Only through contracts routed exclusively through the general contractor
Only through a government-mediated procurement contract
Only a single joint-and-several contract binding all professionals equally
n: Sec. 3.1 and 3.2 describe (1) a single contract between Architect and Owner with sub-consultancy contracts, and (2) separate contracts between the Owner and each of the Architect and the engineering/allied professionals. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 3.1, 3.2)

q: Under Sec. 5.2's formula, what does the variable "R" represent, and what is one example given of an expense includable in R?
o: The Architect's own hourly rate
The Registered Licensed Professional's income tax due
The retention money withheld from the Contractor
Reimbursable expenses, such as transportation/housing/living allowance of consultants and technical staff assigned beyond 100km from the Architect's area of operation
n: The formula section defines R as reimbursable expenses such as transportation, per diem, housing and living allowance of consultants and technical staff assigned to places over 100km from the Architect's area of operation, plus items like extra printing costs, long-distance calls, tests, licenses, fees and taxes. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 5.2 (Formula, definition of R))

q: Per Sec. 7.12, does the Architect assume professional responsibility for inaccuracies in an SPPCC or Cost Estimate he submitted?
o: No, unless glaring errors or discrepancies are clearly evident, since the Architect has no control over labor/material costs or competitive bidding factors
Yes, the Architect guarantees the accuracy of every cost estimate absolutely
No, the Architect is never responsible under any circumstance, even for glaring errors
Yes, but only for Group 1 and Group 2 projects
n: Sec. 7.12 states an SPPCC/Cost Estimate can attain only a certain degree of accuracy, and the Architect does not assume professional responsibility for such estimates unless glaring errors or discrepancies are clearly evident. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 7.12)

q: Sec. 1.1.2 states that resolutions of the Board may call for a foreign architect to work with which of the following?
o: A licensed foreign notary public
A local counterpart Civil Engineer only
A representative of the Department of Foreign Affairs
A local counterpart Architect
n: Sec. 1.1.2 notes that Board resolutions may call for a "local counterpart Architect" to work with any foreign architect offering services in the Philippines. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 1.1.2)

q: Schools, churches, shopping centers and office buildings are classified under which Group?
o: Group 1 - buildings of simplest utilization
Group 2 - buildings of moderate complexity of plan/design
Group 5 - monumental buildings
Group 4 - residences
n: Sec. 4.2 (Group 2) lists Schools, Churches and Religious Facilities, Shopping Centers, and Office Buildings among buildings of moderate complexity of plan/design. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 4.2)

q: If a scale model, 3D model, or walk-thru presentation of the Architect's design is needed (Sec. 7.3), how is this cost treated?
o: Never allowed under SPP Document 202
Recommended by the Architect for Owner approval, paid separately by the Owner and subject to a coordination fee to the Architect
Always included free of charge within the basic professional fee
Charged directly to the Contractor as a construction cost
n: Sec. 7.3 treats scale models, 3D models and walk-thru presentations the same way as Sec. 7.2's other services - recommended by the Architect, paid separately by the Owner, subject to a coordination fee. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 7.3)

q: Which output is specifically produced at the END of the Project Definition Phase, per Sec. 2.1.4?
o: The complete Contract Documents
An initial statement of probable construction cost
The final Certificate of Payment
The Design Development documents
n: Sec. 2.1.4 states that in the Project Definition Phase, the Architect prepares an initial statement of probable construction cost. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 2.1.4)

q: A Group 2 office building undergoes a major renovation, retrofit, and expansion several years after completion. Under Sec. 4.9, how is this renovation project classified?
o: It is no longer classifiable under this SPP
Group 9 - alterations, renovations, rehabilitations, retrofit and expansion/additions to existing buildings belonging to Groups 1 to 5
Group 6, since it reuses the original plans
It reverts automatically to Group 1
n: Sec. 4.9 (Group 9) covers alterations, renovations, rehabilitations, retrofit and expansion/additions to existing buildings belonging to Groups 1 to 5. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 4.9)

q: Per Sec. 7.11, if no Project/Construction Manager is present on site, under whose technical control and supervision does the full-time construction supervisor operate?
o: The General Contractor
The Owner directly, bypassing the Architect
The specialist consultants collectively
The Architect
n: Sec. 7.11 states that if no Project/Construction Manager is present, the full-time construction supervisor is under the technical control and supervision of the Architect, and reports periodically to Owner and Architect. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 7.11)

q: SPP Document 202 (2010 Standards of Professional Practice) governs which of the following?
o: The Code of Ethical Conduct for Architects
Regular Design Services of the Architect
Specialized Architectural Services only
Continuing Professional Development requirements
n: SPP Document 202 is titled "Standard of Professional Practice on Regular Design Services" and covers the scope of services, classification of projects, and compensation methods for an Architect's regular design work. (Source: SPP Document 202, Title)

q: At the start of a commission compensated under the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses method, what must the Architect make known to the Client, per Sec. 5.2?
o: Only the total lump-sum estimate, without any rate breakdown
Nothing - rates may be disclosed only after project completion
The rate of professionals/personnel to be assigned and the multiplier to be applied before agreeing on this method
Only the multiplier, never the individual rates
n: Sec. 5.2 requires the Architect to make known to the Client, at the start of the commission, the rate of professionals/personnel assigned to the project and the multiplier to be applied, before agreeing on this method. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 5.2)

q: Museums, expositions and fair buildings, and mausoleums/memorials/monuments belong to which project classification Group?
o: Group 3 - buildings of exceptional character
Group 5 - monumental buildings and other facilities
Group 8 - projects with extensive detail
Group 10 - opinion or advice
n: Sec. 4.5 (Group 5) covers monumental buildings and other facilities, including Exposition & Fair Buildings and Mausoleums, Memorials & Monuments. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 4.5)

q: A developer plans to build 40 identical row houses on one site using a single set of plans, specifications and related documents. Which project classification Group most specifically describes this?
o: Group 6 - repetitive construction of similar buildings without amending drawings
Group 4 - residences
Group 9 - alterations and renovations
Group 7 - Housing Project involving several residential units on a single site using one (1) set of plans/design
n: Sec. 4.7 (Group 7) specifically describes a Housing Project involving construction of several residential units on a single site using one (1) set of plans/design, specifications, and related documents. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 4.7)

q:
Architect Reyes is engaged under the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses method (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 5.2) for a small renovation involving non-creative, cost-based work. Her own rate is P800/hour for 40 hours logged; her Consultant's rate is P600/hour for 20 hours; her Technical Staff's rate is P300/hour for 60 hours. The parties agree on a multiplier (M) of 2.0 to cover overhead and profit. Reimbursable expenses (R) for the engagement total P15,000.

Applying the agreed multiplier of 2.0, what is Architect Reyes's Fee for this engagement?
n: Fee = Direct Cost x M = P62,000 x 2.0 = P124,000. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 5.2 (Formula: Fee = Direct Cost x M))
scenario: Architect Reyes is engaged under the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses method (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 5.2) for a small renovation involving non-creative, cost-based work. Her own rate is P800/hour for 40 hours logged; her Consultant's rate is P600/hour for 20 hours; her Technical Staff's rate is P300/hour for 60 hours. The parties agree on a multiplier (M) of 2.0 to cover overhead and profit. Reimbursable expenses (R) for the engagement total P15,000.

q: A junior architect tells a client, "Since the design is creative work, I'll just charge you based on my hourly design time multiplied by an overhead factor." Is this consistent with SPP Document 202's Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses method?
o: No - Sec. 5.2 limits this cost-based method to non-creative work only; creative design work's value cannot be measured by time spent
No - this method may never be used for any type of work under any SPP
Yes - this method applies specifically and only to creative design work
Yes - as long as the multiplier used is above 2.5
n: Sec. 5.2 expressly limits the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses method to non-creative, cost-based work, since the value of creative design cannot be measured by hours spent. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 5.2)

q:
Architect Reyes is engaged under the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses method (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 5.2) for a small renovation involving non-creative, cost-based work. Her own rate is P800/hour for 40 hours logged; her Consultant's rate is P600/hour for 20 hours; her Technical Staff's rate is P300/hour for 60 hours. The parties agree on a multiplier (M) of 2.0 to cover overhead and profit. Reimbursable expenses (R) for the engagement total P15,000.

What is the Total Cost of Service that should be charged to the Client?
n: Total Cost of Service = Fee + R = P124,000 + P15,000 = P139,000. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 5.2 (Formula: Total Cost of Service = Fee + R))
scenario: Architect Reyes is engaged under the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses method (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 5.2) for a small renovation involving non-creative, cost-based work. Her own rate is P800/hour for 40 hours logged; her Consultant's rate is P600/hour for 20 hours; her Technical Staff's rate is P300/hour for 60 hours. The parties agree on a multiplier (M) of 2.0 to cover overhead and profit. Reimbursable expenses (R) for the engagement total P15,000.

q: Which method of compensation is described as frequently used where there is a continuing relationship involving a series of Projects, establishing a fixed sum over and above reimbursement for technical time and overhead?
o: Professional Fee Plus Expenses (Sec. 5.3)
Per Diem, Honorarium Plus Reimbursable Expenses (Sec. 5.5)
Percentage of Project Construction Cost (Sec. 5.1)
Lump Sum or Fixed Fee (Sec. 5.4)
n: Sec. 5.3 describes Professional Fee Plus Expenses as frequently used in continuing relationships involving a series of projects, establishing a fixed sum above reimbursement for technical time and overhead. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 5.3)

q: What does the acronym SPPCC stand for in SPP Document 202?
o: Standard Practice for Project Cost Control
Statement of the Probable Project Construction Cost
Summary of Prior Project Construction Contracts
Schedule of Prescribed Professional Compensation and Charges
n: Sec. 2.2.3 defines SPPCC as the Statement of the Probable Project Construction Cost, submitted based on current cost parameters. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 2.2.3)

q: Under either contracting arrangement described in Sec. 3, what happens to the professional responsibilities and civil liabilities of each state-regulated professional involved?
o: They are extinguished once the building permit is issued
They are automatically merged under the Architect's sole liability
They remain separate; the Architect does not assume the responsibilities and liabilities of the other Registered and Licensed Professionals (RLPs)
They are transferred entirely to the Owner
n: Sec. 3 states that in both contracting arrangements, professional responsibilities and civil liabilities of each State-regulated professional remain separate, and the Architect does not assume the responsibilities/liabilities of other RLPs. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 3)

q:
Architect Reyes is engaged under the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses method (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 5.2) for a small renovation involving non-creative, cost-based work. Her own rate is P800/hour for 40 hours logged; her Consultant's rate is P600/hour for 20 hours; her Technical Staff's rate is P300/hour for 60 hours. The parties agree on a multiplier (M) of 2.0 to cover overhead and profit. Reimbursable expenses (R) for the engagement total P15,000.

What is the Direct Cost (AN + CN + TN) of this engagement?
n: Direct cost = AN + CN + TN = (800x40) + (600x20) + (300x60) = 32,000 + 12,000 + 18,000 = P62,000. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 5.2 (Formula: Direct cost = AN + CN + TN))
scenario: Architect Reyes is engaged under the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses method (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 5.2) for a small renovation involving non-creative, cost-based work. Her own rate is P800/hour for 40 hours logged; her Consultant's rate is P600/hour for 20 hours; her Technical Staff's rate is P300/hour for 60 hours. The parties agree on a multiplier (M) of 2.0 to cover overhead and profit. Reimbursable expenses (R) for the engagement total P15,000.

q: What is the effect of a Certificate for Payment issued by the Architect under Sec. 2.6.4?
o: It is a guarantee that the Contractor's workmanship is defect-free for the life of the building
It transfers ownership of the building to the Contractor
It certifies to the Client that the work has progressed to the indicated state and, to the Architect's best knowledge, conforms to the Contract Documents
It automatically extends the Contractor's performance bond
n: Sec. 2.6.4 states these Certificates constitute a certification to the Client that work has progressed to the indicated stage and, to the Architect's best knowledge, that the Contractor's work quality conforms to the Contract Documents. (Source: SPP Document 202, Sec. 2.6.4)
